title: मधेशमा मुख्यमन्त्री दाबी पेसको समय घर्किँदै, सबैको नजर जसपा नेपालमा

No ads found for this position जनकपुरधाम । मधेश प्रदेशमा नयाँ सरकार गठनका लागि गठबन्धन बनाउने समयसीमा घर्किँदै जाँदा पनि सत्ता समीकरणबारे अन्योल कायमै छ । प्रदेश प्रमुख डा. सुरेन्द्र लाभ कर्णले मुख्यमन्त्री नियुक्तिका लागि दाबी पेस गर्न आज दिउँसो ४ बजेसम्मको समय दिए पनि मध्याह्नसम्म कुन दलबीच गठबन्धन बन्ने र कसको नेतृत्वमा सरकार गठन हुने भन्ने टुंगो लागिसकेको छैन । यतिबेला सबैको नजर प्रदेशसभाको सबैभन्दा ठूलो दल जनता समाजवादी पार्टी (जसपा) नेपालमाथि केन्द्रित छ । पार्टीका संरक्षक महन्थ ठाकुर हिजै हवाईमार्गबाट जनकपुरधाम आइपुगेका छन् भने अध्यक्ष उपेन्द्र यादव सडकमार्ग हुँदै जनकपुरधाम पुगेका छन् । दुवै नेता अहिले प्रदेशसभा सदस्यहरूसँग एक–एक गरी भेटघाट र परामर्शमा जुटेका छन् । स्रोतका अनुसार अध्यक्ष यादव र संरक्षक ठाकुरले प्रदेशसभा सदस्यहरूसँग सम्भावित गठबन्धनको समीकरणबारे छलफल गरिरहेका छन् । तर, पार्टीले कुन गठबन्धनलाई समर्थन गर्ने वा कसको नेतृत्वमा सरकार गठन गर्ने भन्ने विषयमा उनीहरूले स्पष्ट धारणा सार्वजनिक गरेका छैनन् । अध्यक्ष यादवको धारणाबारे जिज्ञासा राख्दा जसपा नेपाल मधेश प्रदेश संसदीय दलका नेता सरोजकुमार यादवले बोल्न चाहेनन् । उनले अहिले नै प्रतिक्रिया दिने समय नआइसकेको संक्षिप्त जवाफ दिए । त्यस्तै, जसपा नेपालका नेता मो. जयनुल राइनले पनि गठबन्धनमा जाने वा नजाने विषयमा पार्टीबाट हालसम्म कुनै निर्णय वा निर्देशन आइनसकेको बताए । ‘अहिले केही कुरा खुलेको छैन । समयअनुसार पार्टी अध्यक्षबाट जे निर्देशन आउँछ, हामी त्यही मान्छौँ । अहिले छलफलमै छौँ,’ उनले भने । स्रोतका अनुसार नेकपा (एमाले) सँग गठबन्धन गर्ने सम्भावना भने लगभग टरेको छ । यद्यपि, अब कुन दलसँग सहकार्य गर्ने र कसको नेतृत्वमा सरकार बनाउने भन्ने विषयमा जसपा नेपालले निर्णय गरिसकेको छैन । जसपा नेपालको निर्णयले नै मधेश प्रदेशको आगामी सत्ता समीकरणको दिशा तय गर्ने भएकाले अन्य दलहरू पनि उसको औपचारिक धारणा पर्खिरहेका छन् । प्रदेश प्रमुख डा. कर्णले संविधानको धारा १६८ को उपधारा (२) बमोजिम प्रदेशसभामा प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने दुई वा दुईभन्दा बढी दलको समर्थनमा बहुमत जुटाउन सक्ने प्रदेशसभा सदस्यलाई मुख्यमन्त्री नियुक्तिका लागि दाबी पेस गर्न दिउँसो ४ बजेसम्मको समय सीमा दिएका छन् । गत कात्तिक २८ गते नेपाली कांग्रेसका कृष्णप्रसाद यादवले प्रदेशसभाबाट विश्वासको मत पाउने अवस्था नदेखेपछि सदनबाटै राजीनामाको घोषणा गरेका थिए । उनी हाल कामचलाउ मुख्यमन्त्रीका रूपमा छन् । सत्ता सहकार्यमा रहेका नेकपा (एमाले) र नेपाली कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी (नेकपा) ले एकपछि अर्को गर्दै सरकारलाई दिएको समर्थन फिर्ता लिएपछि यादव नेतृत्वको सरकार अल्पमतमा परेको थियो । मधेश प्रदेशसभामा जसपा नेपाल २८ सांसदसहित सबैभन्दा ठूलो दल छ । एमाले २४ सांसदसहित दोस्रो स्थानमा छ भने नेपाली कांग्रेसका २२, नेकपाका १४ र जनमत पार्टीका १२ सांसद छन् । त्यस्तै, नेपाल सङ्घीय समाजवादी पार्टी, राष्ट्रिय प्रजातन्त्र पार्टी र नागरिक उन्मुक्ति पार्टीका एक–एक जना सांसद छन् । Janakpurdham. As the deadline for forming a coalition to form a new government in Madhesh Province approaches, uncertainty remains over the power equation. Although Province Chief Dr. Surendra Labh Karna has given time till 4 pm today to submit claims for the appointment of Chief Minister, it has not been decided by noon which parties will form a coalition and under whose leadership the government will be formed. All eyes are currently on the Janata Samajwadi Party (JSP) Nepal, the largest party in the provincial assembly . The party's patron, Mahant Thakur, arrived in Janakpurdham by air yesterday, while Chairman Upendra Yadav reached Janakpurdham by road. Both leaders are currently meeting and consulting with the provincial assembly members one by one. According to sources, Chairman Yadav and Patron Thakur are discussing the possible alliance equation with the provincial assembly members. However, they have not made public a clear view on which alliance the party will support or under whose leadership the government will be formed. When asked about Chairman Yadav's opinion, JSP Nepal Madhesh Province Parliamentary Party leader Saroj Kumar Yadav did not want to speak. He gave a brief reply that it was not time to respond now. Similarly, JSP Nepal leader Md. Jayanul Rain also said that no decision or directive has been received from the party so far regarding whether to join the alliance or not. "Nothing has been revealed yet. We will accept whatever directive comes from the party chairman in due course. We are currently in discussions," he said. According to sources, the possibility of forming an alliance with the CPN (UML) has almost disappeared. However, the JSP Nepal has not yet decided which party it will collaborate with and under whose leadership it will form the government. Since the decision of the JSP Nepal will determine the direction of the future power equation in the Madhesh province, other parties are also waiting for its formal opinion. Provincial Chief Dr. Karna has given a deadline of 4 pm to the Provincial Assembly members who can muster a majority with the support of two or more parties represented in the Provincial Assembly as per Article 168 (2) of the Constitution to submit their claims for the appointment of Chief Minister. On November 11, Krishna Prasad Yadav of the Nepali Congress announced his resignation from the House after failing to secure a vote of confidence from the Provincial Assembly . He is currently serving as the acting Chief Minister. The Yadav-led government was in a minority after the ruling coalition partners, the CPN (UML) and the Nepali Communist Party (NCP), withdrew their support one after another . JSP Nepal is the largest party in the Madhesh Provincial Assembly with 28 MPs. UML is in second place with 24 MPs, while Nepali Congress has 22 MPs, NCP has 14 MPs, and Janmat Party has 12 MPs. Similarly, Nepal Federal Socialist Party, Rastriya Prajatantra Party, and Nagarik Unmukti Party have one MP each.

As the deadline for forming a coalition to form a new government in Madhesh Province approaches, uncertainty remains over the power equation. The party's patron, Mahant Thakur, arrived in Janakpurdham by air yesterday, while Chairman Upendra Yadav reached Janakpurdham by road. Both leaders are currently meeting and consulting with the provincial assembly members one by one. According to sources, Chairman Yadav and Patron Thakur are discussing the possible alliance equation with the provincial assembly members. Similarly, Nepal Federal Socialist Party, Rastriya Prajatantra Party, and Nagarik Unmukti Party have one MP each.

As the deadline for forming a coalition to form a new government in Madhesh Province approaches, uncertainty remains over the power equation. Although Province Chief Dr. Surendra Labh Karna has given time till 4 pm today to submit claims for the appointment of Chief Minister, it has not been decided by noon which parties will form a coalition and under whose leadership the government will be formed. All eyes are currently on the Janata Samajwadi Party (JSP) Nepal, the largest party in the provincial assembly . The party's patron, Mahant Thakur, arrived in Janakpurdham by air yesterday, while Chairman Upendra Yadav reached Janakpurdham by road. Both leaders are currently meeting and consulting with the provincial assembly members one by one. According to sources, Chairman Yadav and Patron Thakur are discussing the possible alliance equation with the provincial assembly members. However, they have not made public a clear view on which alliance the party will support or under whose leadership the government will be formed. When asked about Chairman Yadav's opinion, JSP Nepal Madhesh Province Parliamentary Party leader Saroj Kumar Yadav did not want to speak. He gave a brief reply that it was not time to respond now. He is currently serving as the acting Chief Minister. The Yadav-led government was in a minority after the ruling coalition partners, the CPN (UML) and the Nepali Communist Party (NCP), withdrew their support one after another . JSP Nepal is the largest party in the Madhesh Provincial Assembly with 28 MPs. UML is in second place with 24 MPs, while Nepali Congress has 22 MPs, NCP has 14 MPs, and Janmat Party has 12 MPs. Although Province Chief Dr. Surendra Labh Karna has given time till 4 pm today to submit claims for the appointment of Chief Minister, it has not been decided by noon which parties will form a coalition and under whose leadership the government will be formed. All eyes are currently on the Janata Samajwadi Party (JSP) Nepal, the largest party in the provincial assembly . The party's patron, Mahant Thakur, arrived in Janakpurdham by air yesterday, while Chairman Upendra Yadav reached Janakpurdham by road. Both leaders are currently meeting and consulting with the provincial assembly members one by one. According to sources, Chairman Yadav and Patron Thakur are discussing the possible alliance equation with the provincial assembly members. However, they have not made public a clear view on which alliance the party will support or under whose leadership the government will be formed. When asked about Chairman Yadav's opinion, JSP Nepal Madhesh Province Parliamentary Party leader Saroj Kumar Yadav did not want to speak. He gave a brief reply that it was not time to respond now. Similarly, JSP Nepal leader Md. Jayanul Rain also said that no decision or directive has been received from the party so far regarding whether to join the alliance or not. "Nothing has been revealed yet. We will accept whatever directive comes from the party chairman in due course. We are currently in discussions," he said. According to sources, the possibility of forming an alliance with the CPN (UML) has almost disappeared. However, the JSP Nepal has not yet decided which party it will collaborate with and under whose leadership it will form the government. Since the decision of the JSP Nepal will determine the direction of the future power equation in the Madhesh province, other parties are also waiting for its formal opinion. Provincial Chief Dr. Karna has given a deadline of 4 pm to the Provincial Assembly members who can muster a majority with the support of two or more parties represented in the Provincial Assembly as per Article 168 (2) of the Constitution to submit their claims for the appointment of Chief Minister. On November 11, Krishna Prasad Yadav of the Nepali Congress announced his resignation from the House after failing to secure a vote of confidence from the Provincial Assembly . He is currently serving as the acting Chief Minister. The Yadav-led government was in a minority after the ruling coalition partners, the CPN (UML) and the Nepali Communist Party (NCP), withdrew their support one after another . JSP Nepal is the largest party in the Madhesh Provincial Assembly with 28 MPs. UML is in second place with 24 MPs, while Nepali Congress has 22 MPs, NCP has 14 MPs, and Janmat Party has 12 MPs. Similarly, Nepal Federal Socialist Party, Rastriya Prajatantra Party, and Nagarik Unmukti Party have one MP each.
